newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta stock exchange ends slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Malta stock exchange ends slightly lower.

text.p: The Malta stock exchange closed its once-weekly trading session slightly lower on Wednesday, with trade dominated by institutional investors in government stocks.
Trading reached just over 5.56 million Maltese pounds ($14.5 million).
There were 94 deals, of which 66 were in fixed income securities and 28 in equities.
Trading in government stocks accounted for just over 5.5 million pounds, with investors homing in mainly on the 7.5 percent MGS 2011, which is the longest term bond.
There was 4,000 pounds worth of business in Mid-Med Bank's unsecured loan stock 2005 spread over seven deals at an average price of 100.1. The current yield for this bond is 7.24 percent.
Trading in equities reached 48,000 pounds and the share index shed five points to 982.17.
The average share price in Bank of Valletta remained unchanged at 123 cents, with total turnover reaching 21,000 pounds.
Trading in Mid-Med Bank shares reached 5,505 pounds, with the average share price dropping three cents to 149.8 cents.

At the same time, 14,965 Lombard Bank Malta shares were traded at an average 140 cents per share, unchanged. In Middle Sea Insurance, 400 shares were traded for an average 122.7 cents per share, up seven mils.
